Let $1\leq d_1<d_2$ and $k\geq 3$. Does there exist an integer $r$ such that if $B=\{b_1<\cdots\}$ is a lacunary sequence of positive integers with $b_{i+1}\geq rb_i$ then there exists a sequence of positive integers $A=\{a_1<\cdots\}$ such that\[d_1\leq a_{i+1}-a_i\leq d_2\]for all $i\geq 1$ and $(kA)\cap B=\emptyset$, where $kA$ is the $k$-fold sumset?
#1112: [ErGr80,p.18]
additive combinatorics
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] noted that if $B=\{b_1<b_2<\cdots\}$ with $b_1\geq 5$ and $b_{i+1}\geq 2b_i$ then there is a set $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ with $2\leq a_{k+1}-a_k\leq 3$ for all $k$ such that $(A+A)\cap B=\emptyset$. Bollobás, Hegyvári, and Jin [BHJ97] showed that such an $A$ must exist if $b_{i+1}\geq 2b_i-O(1)$, and that this is best possible.
Erdős and Graham go on to say 'whether such behavior can hold for $A+A+A$ (or more summands) is not known'. The above question is my best interpretation of what they intended.
Bollobás, Hegyvári, and Jin [BHJ97] provide a negative answer in that, for any sequence of integers $1\leq r_1<r_2<\cdots$, there is a $B$ as above with $b_{i+1}\geq r_ib_i$ such that $(A+A+A)\cap B\neq\emptyset$ for any $A$ with $2\leq a_{i+1}-a_i\leq 3$.
They define, more generally, $r_k(d_1,d_2)$ as the smallest $r$ (if it exists) such that if $b_{i+1}\geq rb_i$ then there exists $A$ with $d_1\leq a_{i+1}-a_i\leq d_2$ such that $(kA)\cap B=\emptyset$, where $kA$ is the $k$-fold sumset.
It follows from the above results that $r_2(2,3)=2$ and that $r_3(2,3)$ does not exist. Chen [Ch00] proved that $r_2(a,b)\leq 2$ for any integers $a<b$ with $b\neq 2a$, and that $r_2(a,2a)\geq 2$ for all integers $a$. The more general question of existence of $r_k(a,b)$ for $k\geq 3$ remains open.
Some further technical non-existence results are given by Tang and Yang [TaYa21].
[Note the stated problem is a generous interpretation of a very ambiguous remark in [ErGr80], so it might be more appropriate to call this a problem 'inspired by Erdős and Graham'.]

 A proposed resolution of #1112, for all $k \ge 3$. Posted here for scrutiny.
The page notes that "the more general question of existence of $r_k(a,b)$ for $k \ge 3$ remains open." I believe the answer is yes if and only if $d_2 \ge k+1$, though this has not yet been checked by anyone but me, so I would be very grateful for corrections. Writing $r_k(d_1,d_2)$ for the least valid ratio $r$ when one exists, the claim is:
Dichotomy (claimed). For every $k \ge 3$ and $1 \le d_1 < d_2$,\[
r_k(d_1,d_2)\ \text{exists} \iff d_2 \ge k+1.
\]Existence ($d_2 \ge k+1$). A Beatty / nested-interval construction places $A$ so that its $k$-fold sumset threads the gaps a lacunary $B$ must leave, giving the explicit bound $r_k(d_1,d_2) \le 192\,d_2$ (the constant is not optimized; $d_1$ does not affect the threshold).
Non-existence ($d_2 \le k$), strong form. No growth condition on $B$ suffices: for every sequence $r_1 \le r_2 \le \cdots$ there is a single $B$ with $b_{i+1} \ge r_i b_i$ such that $(kA) \cap B \ne \emptyset$ for every admissible $A$. A word-combinatorial analysis (balanced words, Morse–Hedlund, Sturmian ladders) with an amortized "slot" argument reduces this to one finite additive-combinatorics lemma (SHARP): every finite $G \subset \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ with $|G| \ge 3$, $\gcd(G) = 1$, $\max(G) = M$ admits a multiset of at most $M-1$ of its elements whose subset sums contain $M$ consecutive integers.
What gives me some confidence to post this at all: the whole argument, all three theorems including the strong non-existence form, is formalized in Lean 4 (sorry-free, no native_decide, depending only on the three standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and reproducible with a single lake build. The one thing a formalization cannot self-certify is that the Lean statement faithfully encodes the problem as posed here; I set out that correspondence, definition by definition, in a Lean statement faithfulness discussion. That bridge, together with the prose, is exactly where I would most value expert review.
Full proof, Lean sources, and paper.

A full proof 
claimed by Johan Land (using Fable 5, Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5 Pro).
 Summary:
 Note: Proof previously discussed in the comment section before this "proof claim" functionality was added to the site.
Briefly:
For $k \ge 3$, $r_k(d_1,d_2)$ exists iff $d_2 \ge k+1$, with $r_k \le 192,d_2$ - independently of $d_1$. Existence: a Beatty sequence with slope $\gamma \in (k, d_2)$ confines $kA$ to width-$k$ windows, and a nested-interval argument steers $\gamma$ past every element of a lacunary $B$. Non-existence: a single diagonal $B$ works once every admissible $kA$ contains a full congruence class eventually; this reduces, via word combinatorics for two-letter gap alphabets (Sturmian case included) and a subset-sum lemma for larger ones - every finite $G$ with $\gcd(G)=1$, $|G|\ge 3$ admits a multiset of at most $\max G - 1$ elements whose subset sums contain $\max G$ consecutive integers.
Context:
Everything is verified in Lean (see link below).

I've structured a repo to ease consumption of the proof: https://github.com/beetree/math_erdos_1112
